verificationContext.gitDiffSummary: Manual review authorized by the user. OPT-01 preserves summary reachability with multi-source BFS and explicit canonical paths; OPT-02 removes only adjacency-local sorting because append order follows globally sorted uniqueRelations; OPT-03 retains full matching/ranking/totalMatches and delays public projection, matchedFields, and bounded evidence until after limit selection. LSP reports no diagnostics for all four changed TypeScript files. Focused tests (40), full tests (163 files / 2395 tests), build, typecheck, lint, semantic validation, and diff checks pass. The earlier validation command raced a parallel build and briefly saw a missing dist entry; validation was rerun successfully after build completion.

directions.opportunity: Default impact computes canonical paths that its result deliberately omits.
directions.impact: Remove path-array copying, canonical tie-breaking, and path-result sorting from summary-only calls. A multi-source breadth-first traversal computes the required union of reachable identities without retaining paths or repeating traversal separately for every focus.
evidence: src/commands/arch/impact.ts:61-91 copies path prefixes and compares serialized candidate paths; lines 160-172 perform this work unconditionally for every focus.
src/commands/arch/impact.ts:230-249 uses reachable identities for the induced relationship subgraph and summary, but exposes relations and relationPaths only when options.paths is truthy.
The arch-impact Delta explicitly separates summary-only defaults from --paths while retaining depth-bounded traversal and independent refinement context.
A read-only in-memory comparison against the current canonicalPaths helper passed 17,920 combinations covering all 512 directed three-node graphs, nonempty focus subsets, and depths 0-4.
directions.recommendation: Keep the existing canonical-path implementation for explicit path requests; use identity-only multi-source BFS for the default projection.
directions.keyDesign: After the existing validation and adjacency construction, branch on the same options.paths condition used by the result. For summary-only calls, initialize visited and frontier with all deduplicated focus identities, traverse incoming and outgoing adjacency one layer at a time up to depth, and stop when the frontier is empty. Leave refinement construction and induced-subgraph filtering shared and unchanged. For explicit paths, retain per-focus canonicalPaths and its current tie-breaking.
preservationConstraints: Preserve option validation, model loading, root checks, sorted focus validation, endpoint validation, diagnostic text, and their error order; do not skip these at depth zero.
Preserve the union of identities reachable within depth from any focus, including duplicate-focus elimination, disconnected focuses, cycles, self-loops, and all declared relationship kinds.
Do not seed relationship traversal with refinement ancestors or descendants. Refinement context remains separately computed, including full ancestor chains and depth-bounded descendants.

Keep relationships selected by both endpoints belonging to the reachable union, including cross-focus edges and edges not used by traversal; preserve relation counts, per-kind counts, and deterministic output ordering.
Default and paths:false outputs must still omit relations and relationPaths entirely. Explicit paths retain canonical direction, shortest-path tie-breaking, ordering, and text/JSON output.
Retain current accepted numeric depth semantics and exhausted-frontier termination; introduce no cache, file writes, public API changes, or model changes.
implementationOutline: Add a private identity-only traversal in the existing implementation file, using sets/frontiers rather than path records.
Use it only for summary-only calls; retain the existing explicit-path branch and common downstream projection.
Extend the owning impact tests with equality between default output and expanded output after removing its two optional fields.
validation: Extend test/commands/arch-impact.test.ts:57-107 to compare complete shared projections across both modes, not merely field presence.
Exercise multiple and duplicate focuses, overlapping neighborhoods, cross-focus edges, cycles, self-loops, depth zero, empty adjacency, and huge depth with early exhaustion.
Retain canonical tie-breaking and permutation coverage at test/commands/arch-impact.test.ts:110-148, high-degree/self-loop coverage at 160-190, and refinement/error/read-only coverage at 194-245.
Run the owning impact suite and test/integration/arch-command.test.ts after implementation; inspect that summary-only execution never calls canonicalPaths or constructs path-step arrays.
directions.priorityReason: First because it removes an entire unused path-computation phase and repeated per-focus traversal, a larger provable reduction than redundant sorting or discarded search-result formatting.

directions.opportunity: Adjacency lists are sorted again even though they are built as ordered subsequences of an already sorted relationship collection.
directions.impact: Eliminate one redundant sort per adjacency list and its comparator/key-string work for both default and explicit-path calls.
evidence: src/commands/arch/impact.ts:138-140 deduplicates relationships and sorts uniqueRelations with compareRelations.
src/commands/arch/impact.ts:150-156 visits that sorted array once and appends each relationship to its endpoint lists without reordering; the endpoint Set inserts a self-loop once.
src/commands/arch/impact.ts:158 sorts each resulting subsequence using the identical comparator.
The in-memory check confirmed that every adjacency list across all 512 directed three-node graphs was already equal to its sorted copy.
directions.recommendation: Remove only the redundant per-adjacency sort and document that list order is inherited from uniqueRelations.
directions.keyDesign: Make the existing globally sorted uniqueRelations collection the ordering owner. Continue append-only adjacency construction with the same endpoint deduplication; consumers receive exactly the same relationship sequence without another sorting pass.
preservationConstraints: Retain relationKey deduplication, its current duplicate-selection behavior, the global compareRelations sort, and endpoint validation order.
Retain append order and the Set around source/target so self-loops are not inserted twice.
Do not substitute locale-dependent comparison or reorder canonical path candidates, emitted relationships, or error checks.
Do not remove unrelated child, refinement, result, or summary sorts; preserve all public results and side effects.
implementationOutline: Delete the per-list sorting loop at the current line 158.
Add a short invariant comment at adjacency construction explaining why each list is already sorted.
Keep this change independent of the summary-only traversal optimization so either can be verified separately.
validation: Run test/commands/arch-impact.test.ts, especially canonical-path permutations at 110-148, high-degree/self-loop ordering at 160-190, and cross-locale output at 248-263.
Compare complete explicit-path output before and after the change on shuffled relationship inputs, multiple kinds, incoming edges, and self-loops.
Confirm by source inspection that adjacency construction remains an append-only projection of globally sorted uniqueRelations.
directions.priorityReason: Second: smaller benefit than removing unused canonical paths, but the preservation proof is especially narrow and implementation cost is lower than restructuring search projection.

directions.opportunity: Search constructs public evidence projections for every match before --limit discards excess matches.
directions.impact: For matches excluded by the limit, avoid matched-field Set construction/sorting, bounded-evidence string processing, and public-result object allocation. Matching, complete candidate ordering, and totalMatches remain unchanged.
evidence: src/commands/arch/search.ts:80-96 sorts evidence and immediately constructs matchedFields and bounded evidence for every matching Element.
src/commands/arch/search.ts:99-106 sorts all matches and applies the limit only afterward.
The arch-search Delta requires limiting after complete candidate sorting, but does not require constructing presentation evidence for candidates that will not be returned.
test/commands/arch-search.test.ts:74-93 owns rank/identity ordering, totalMatches, limit behavior, and bounded Unicode evidence.
directions.recommendation: Separate internal ranked candidates from public match projection, applying the existing output transformation only to selected candidates.
directions.keyDesign: Retain each candidate's declaration reference, sorted RankedEvidence array, and strongest rank. Preserve the existing global rank/identity sort and totalMatches calculation, then slice by limit. Only afterward construct element identity/title/parent, matchedFields, and bounded evidence using the existing transformation and boundedEvidence helper.
preservationConstraints: Preserve query trimming, empty-query and invalid-limit errors, model-read timing, case conversion, exact versus substring matching, and all current rank values.
Continue scanning all Elements and Sections and fully sorting all candidate matches before limiting; preserve totalMatches and unbounded-search behavior.
Preserve evidence ordering by rank, field, and original unbounded text. Do not sort by excerpts or deduplicate evidence: exact-title and substring-title evidence may both exist.
Preserve matchedFields ordering and uniqueness, candidate multiplicity, stable equal-key ordering, and exact identity/title/parent values.
Keep boundedEvidence's current UTF-16 length/index behavior, ellipses, centering, and query handling byte-for-byte; this is not a Unicode or matching-behavior redesign.
Preserve JSON field boundaries, text formatting, diagnostics, read-only behavior, and complete semantic content behind explicit query.
implementationOutline: Introduce an internal ranked-candidate shape in the existing file without changing exported interfaces.
Move only public match construction from the discovery loop to the mapping after sorting and slicing; retain evidence sorting and rank derivation initially.
Extend the owning tests to compare every limited result with the corresponding prefix of the unlimited result.
validation: Run test/commands/arch-search.test.ts and search coverage in test/integration/arch-command.test.ts.

Compare limited and unlimited results for exact identity/title matches, title substrings, long Definitions, repeated Section evidence, tied identities, no matches, and limits below/equal to/above match count.
Assert identical totalMatches, evidence multiplicity/order, matchedFields, excerpts, diagnostics, and formatted text for selected candidates.
Verify structurally that boundedEvidence and public projection construction occur only after candidate selection; avoid timing-dependent performance assertions.
directions.priorityReason: Third: statically avoids discarded projection work, but has a smaller benefit and a broader data-flow edit than the preceding directions.
